notes:
User is planning a month-long workout routine and wants to complete a 10K by the end of summer. They are a complete beginner at running but do regular gym cardio and outdoor activity. Current baseline: three 30-minute lunch-break walks weekly. They can dedicate 4–5 hours weekly to training. A gradual 12-week beginner plan was discussed; they especially preferred adding only 1–2 minutes of jogging per week during weeks 5–8. They value manageable pacing, injury/burnout prevention, small wins, and patience.

They have been consistent at the gym for about three months and have now lost 10 lb total. They are doing well with workouts and diet, want an unspecified goal weight by the end of summer, use a fitness app, and previously reported averaging 2,500 calories burned weekly. They value ongoing encouragement, progress tracking, and accountability, and hope to find a similarly paced beginner running buddy through online platforms or local groups.

Current core work includes planks and Russian twists. They especially like/plan to add Pallof presses and bird dogs, and now want oblique-specific variety such as side planks, woodchops/cable rotations, Pallof press with rotation, side crunches, and dynamic planks. Other lower-body suggestions include step-ups, twisting lunges, calf raises, and glute bridges. Strength training 2–3 times weekly is appropriate alongside running.

They are also working on flexibility and range of motion, especially hamstrings and hip flexors. They already do yoga and Pilates but want greater consistency. They plan to use dynamic stretching/warmups, hold static stretches longer without bouncing, and try yoga blocks, straps, or bands. Advice should emphasize consistency, easy progression, mobility work, and form.

For workout motivation, they want high-energy cardio playlists and appreciate genre variety (hip-hop, pop, rock, electronic/dance) and music matched to workout intensity. Energy-management priorities are balanced pre-workout nutrition, hydration, moderate caffeine if desired, pacing/breathing, adequate sleep, recovery, and balanced post-workout carbs/protein; avoid treating supplements as necessary. Hydrate beforehand, sip as needed during short/hot runs, monitor pale-yellow urine, and consider electrolytes for runs over an hour.
